children: Oil prices extend gains, with Brent crude pushing past $100 a barrel as fresh clashes between the U.S. and Iran deepen concerns over supply disruptions and the impact of a prolonged war on the broader economy. Brent crude rise 0.8% to $102 a barrel, while WTI futures are up 1.4% to $97.38 a barrel. Traders now await the release of weekly inventory data from the Energy Information Administration later on Thursday, with a particular focus on distillate stock changes given the current tightness in global diesel markets. OPEC and the IEA will also release their monthly oil reports this week. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
